newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Mexican leader in Singapore to boost business ties.
newsitem.headline: Mexican leader in Singapore to boost business ties.

text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo arrived in Singapore on Tuesday for a three-day visit aimed at bolstering trade and business links between two nations on opposite sides of the Pacific Ocean.

Zedillo arrived as the head of a 70-man delegation which includes Foreign Minister Jose Angel Gurria Trevino, Commerce and Industrial Development Minister Herminio Blanco Mendoza and top Mexican businessmen.

"President Zedillo chose to come to Singapore because it is the centre of gravity in Southeast Asia," Juan de Villafranca, Mexico's ambassador to the city-state, told reporters in a briefing last Friday ahead of the visit here.
The Mexican President will meet with Singapore President Ong Teng Cheong, Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and senior minister Lee Kuan Yew during his visit.
He will also deliver a speech on Mexico's expanding ties with the Asia-Pacific region on Wednesday before a group of leading Singaporean businessmen.
Mexican officials said two projects by Singaporean investors in Mexico worth US$65 million will be signed during Zedillo's visit.

The Port of Singapore Authority has also joined a Mexican construction company in a bid for the port of Ensenada, which is being privatised by Mexico and is near the towns of Tijuana and Mexicali, bordering the United States.

Zedillo will leave on Thursday aboard a private jet for South Korea. He had earlier visited China and then went to the Philippines to attend the leaders' summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
